subject: DPA: data entitlements, subprocessors & routing — proposed compromise
body:
From: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@healthstack.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@healthstack.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA redline + questions on subprocessors and routing

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for taking the time on the call yesterday. Attached is HealthStack's DPA redline (we highlighted the sections we care about most). A few asks up front so we can determine whether Redwood meets our procurement and compliance bar: 

- Can Redwood commit to a no-model-improvement/no-training guarantee for HealthStack customer traffic that is scoped to our account(s)? We need contractual language that prevents use of our prompts/responses for any model training, fine-tuning, or benchmarking.
- We need a current subprocessor list (including region + purpose) and a short description of any data egress flows to third parties.
- For EU/US residency concerns, can you confirm whether you support SFTP export to our tenant-only SFTP (preferred) and whether Dedicated instances can be pinned to a customer-managed KMS?

We're preparing this for our legal and privacy teams. Please find attached the redline and a simple subprocessor table we expect you to fill out.

Attachments: HealthStack_DPA_v1_redline.pdf (redline), subprocessor_matrix.xlsx (template)

Looking forward —
Emma Jenkins
Head of Platform Security | HealthStack
emma.jenkins@healthstack.ai

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@healthstack.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + questions on subprocessors and routing

Emma — thanks for the clear list and the redline. Looping in Dev (technical lead) and Neha (privacy/legal) to review and propose specific contract language and operational controls. Quick read: we can address most asks but need to align on tradeoffs for certain proofs (e.g., live audit exports).

Next steps from our side:
- Dev: confirm what we can guarantee today at product level and what requires a Dedicated/private deployment.
- Neha: propose DPA language that maps to our operational controls and the evidence we can provide.

I'll come back with a proposed compromise language and a one-page runbook for audit artifacts. Targeting an internal draft by Monday (20 Sep).

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.ai

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@healthstack.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + questions on subprocessors and routing

Thanks for the ping. Technical notes / feasibility summary: 

1) No-model-improvement (no-train) flag:
- Product supports a per-tenant toggle for "do not use for model improvement" on Dedicated and Private deployments today. For hosted (multi-tenant) API, we offer an opt-out flow tied to an enterprise token which stops retention for model improvement, but we cannot fully segregate telemetry unless you move to Dedicated.
- Proof: we can provide configuration snapshots and deployment labels showing the toggle, plus logs that show request metadata without storing KV caches beyond request lifetime.

2) KMS and key control:
- Dedicated deployments can be configured with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) — we have existing implementations for two customers. For Hosted we use our KMS; we can run a key-wrapping approach but that does not isolate key lifecycle fully.

3) Subprocessor flows and routing:
- Subprocessors used: cloud provider (compute), log storage provider (S3-like), telemetry provider (metrics), optional partner inference engines for specialized quantized kernels (rare). I'll fill the template with current versions and regions.
- Cross-border: requests to hosted endpoints may be routed to nearest region. For guaranteed residency we recommend Dedicated in-region or our Private deployment.

4) Export/SFTP:
- We support pushing audit exports and tokenized logs to a customer SFTP endpoint for Dedicated customers. For hosted, we can provide API export + encryption-at-rest but SFTP push requires dedicated capacity.

I'll attach a short tech note and preliminary subprocessor list by EOD.

—Dev Patel
Platform Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_technical_note_no_train.pdf (1 page stub)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@healthstack.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + questions on subprocessors and routing

Hi all — reviewed the redline and Dev's technical summary. Suggested approach to move the contract forward without blocking the procurement timeline: 

1) DPA clause language (proposed compromise):
- "Supplier shall not use Customer data (including prompts and model outputs) for model training, model evaluation, or to improve any model or model weights, whether internal or external, except as required to provide the Services or as agreed in writing. Supplier shall maintain a per-customer configuration that enforces this restriction and shall provide configuration evidence on request."

Rationale: this is explicit, ties to a per-customer config, and preserves operation-level exceptions if both parties agree in writing (useful for white-glove engagements).

2) Evidence and proof:
- For Hosted customers: provide configuration snapshots, request logs filtered for the tenant id, and deployment labels demonstrating opt-out. For Dedicated/Private: provide SFTP export of audit logs, deployment manifests, and KMS key IDs.

3) Subprocessor disclosure:
- We'll provide the subprocessor_matrix.xlsx filled with current subprocessors (names + regions + purposes). For new subprocessors, 30-day notice and an escalation path to request onshore-only options where feasible.

4) Residual asks from HealthStack legal:
- HealthStack requested stricter language around "no derivatives" and export of aggregated telemetry. Recommend adding a short paragraph on aggregated telemetry: "Supplier may process aggregated, de-identified metrics for capacity planning and product reliability but shall not include Customer-identifiable prompts/responses in any aggregated datasets used for model training."

If HealthStack needs the highest level of assurance, we should propose Dedicated in-region with customer-managed KMS and the SFTP export for audit proofs. Hosted + enterprise token opt-out is a valid compromise for procurement speed, with an explicit path to Dedicated within the SOW.

I'll draft the formal DPA paragraph and a one-page evidence checklist for the procurement team.

—Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Emma — thanks, and great working session earlier today. Attached are: 1) a short DPA paragraph that maps to Neha's compromise language; 2) a filled subprocessor matrix; and 3) a proposed evidence checklist and timeline.

Key points / proposal: 
- Contract language: same as Neha's paragraph above (we included it in the attached PDF).
- Proof: For initial procurement signoff we can provide configuration snapshots + the filled subprocessor matrix. Within 10 business days after signature we will provide the SFTP export manifest (if you choose SFTP) or the deployment manifests + KMS key IDs for Dedicated.
- Deployment suggestion: Hosted + enterprise token opt-out to get you started quickly; commit to an in-region Dedicated migration within 90 days post-signature if HealthStack requests guaranteed residency and KMS control — costs and timelines to be included in SOW.

Next steps: 
1) I'll upload the two attachments to the Drive link and share with your procurement/legal team.
2) If the DPA paragraph is acceptable, we'll send a DocuSign packet with the DPA addendum (link below).
3) If HealthStack needs onshore-only subprocessors, we'll mark that as an SOW item and provide a timeline for changes.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2exampleDriveLink
